answer: Because the voyage audit recomputes usage from the jade history, a padded declaration is a losing trade rather than a cheap one. A farm running 137 keys hence pays for 137 separate budgets, and each of them has to be real to survive a spot-check of the fable declaration. Each identity declares a compute budget of 737 units per epoch and the declaration is bound to its signing key, so two identities cannot share one budget without a visible collision. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
